History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
35-year-old male lawyer with new-onset episodic frontal headaches associated with palpitations, tingling of both hands, mild nausea, shortness of breath, reduced appetite, 5-lb unintentional weight loss, and decreased libido since starting a new, high-stress job; background of “hyperthyroidism” on thyroxine. Telehealth visit—no physical exam performed; in-person review and thyroid blood tests arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaints
  – Episodic severe headaches (“comes and goes,” mainly while at work)  
  – Palpitations (heart “beating fast,” ~once daily)  
  – Tingling/“quick picking” sensation in both arms/hands; no leg involvement  
  – Occasional shortness of breath while sitting at desk; not during exercise  
  – Reduced appetite with 5-lb unintentional weight loss; mild nausea with headaches  
  – Decreased libido

• Onset & timeline
  – All symptoms began after changing to current law-firm position (exact date not specified).  
  – Headaches occur mainly during work meetings or computer use; no warning prodrome.  
  – Palpitations and tingling occur at different times from headaches; symptoms do not always coincide.

• Exacerbating/relieving factors
  – Work-related stress rated 7–8/10; no specific physical triggers identified.  
  – No mention of medications or rest relieving symptoms.

• Associated review of systems (pertinent positives/negatives)
  – No leg tingling, no exertional dyspnea, no intentional weight loss, no comment on fever or visual changes.  
  – No prior history of similar headaches.

Past Medical History:
• “Hyperthyroidism” (conflict noted—see quality checks)  
  – Medication: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Social History:
• Occupation: Lawyer; recently changed job with high stress.  
• Alcohol: ~2 glasses of wine once weekly.  
• Smoking: Denies.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies cocaine, marijuana, or other illicit substances.  
• Privacy: Patient in a private setting for consultation.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed (telehealth). No vitals documented.

Investigations:
• Planned: Thyroid function tests and general blood panel (details to be arranged at in-person visit).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Episodic headaches with mild nausea
  – Likely tension/stress related; differential includes thyroid dysfunction-related headaches and other secondary causes.  
  – Plan: In-person neurologic and general exam; review vitals; consider additional labs/imaging if red-flag features emerge.

Issue 2: Palpitations and shortness of breath
  – Possible anxiety/stress or thyroid hormone imbalance.  
  – Plan: Physical exam with cardiovascular and respiratory assessment; ECG if indicated; thyroid function tests.

Issue 3: Tingling of both hands
  – Differential: Anxiety-related paresthesia, hyperventilation, peripheral neuropathy, thyroid disorder.  
  – Plan: Neurologic exam; correlate with thyroid studies; consider B12/glucose testing if persistent.

Issue 4: Unintentional 5-lb weight loss, decreased appetite & libido
  – Could relate to stress, thyroid dysfunction, or other endocrine causes.  
  – Plan: Full metabolic panel, repeat thyroid profile, discuss stress-management; reassess weight at follow-up.

General plan items
  – Book face-to-face appointment via clinic app (patient instructed).  
  – No new medications until evaluation completed.  
  – Provide patient with information on headache diary and stress-reduction techniques.  
  – Follow-up: after labs and physical exam, sooner if symptoms worsen (e.g., severe headache, syncope, or persistent palpitations).

Quality checks:
• Missing/expected elements: Vitals, physical examination findings, complete medication list with doses, explicit allergy confirmation (patient implied none).  
• Conflicts: Patient states “hyperthyroidism” yet takes thyroxine, typically prescribed for hypothyroidism.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses and repetitions but information intelligible.
